messages.content: Change the settings of my air conditioner. Set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22 degrees Celsius. Enable the power save mode and set the high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now? For everything else

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to change settings of their air conditioner. They want to set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22°C. Enable power save mode and set high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now. For everything else, presumably keep defaults or unspecified. We need to call the ThinQ_Connect function with appropriate body. The function expects a dictionary with optional keys: airConJobMode, windStrength, monitoringEnabled, airCleanOperationMode, airConOperationMode, powerSaveEnabled, targetTemperature, relativeHourToStop, relativeMinuteToStop, relativeHourToStart, relativeMinuteToStart.

We want to set airConJobMode to "COOL" (default is COOL anyway). windStrength to "HIGH". powerSaveEnabled to true. targetTemperature to 22. relativeHourToStart to 1. relativeMinuteToStart to 30. For everything else, we can omit or set to defaults. The function signature: ThinQ_Connect(body: { ... }). So we need to call the function with body containing those fields. The user didn't specify anything about airConOperationMode; default is POWER_OFF. But maybe we want to turn it on? The user says "Change the settings of my air conditioner. Set it to cool mode with a target temperature of 22 degrees Celsius. Enable the power save mode and set the high wind strength. Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now? For everything else". They didn't mention turning it on. But they want to start in 1 hour and 30 minutes. That implies we want to schedule it to start. The airConOperationMode might be left as default POWER_OFF. But maybe we want to set it to POWER_ON? The user didn't explicitly say to turn it on. They said "Start in 1 hour and 30 minutes from now?" That might mean schedule start. So we set relativeHourToStart=1, relativeMinuteToStart=30. We don't set airConOperationMode. So we leave it default. We also don't set relativeHourToStop or relativeMinuteToStop. We don't set monitoringEnabled or airCleanOperationMode. So we just set the ones we care about.

Thus we call ThinQ_Connect with body: { airConJobMode: "COOL", windStrength: "HIGH", powerSaveEnabled: true, targetTemperature: 22, relativeHourToStart: 1, relativeMinuteToStart: 30 }.

We need to produce a JSON object with the function call. The function name is "ThinQ_Connect". The arguments: body: { ... }.

We need to output the function call. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we just call the function.
